section_summary: This section begins with the concluding chapters of the 1947 report of the U.S. Scientific Advisory Group, which analyzes Japanese higher education, university administration, and industrial laboratories, recommending the creation of an Advisory Council and a Commission on Higher Education and Research, accompanied by General Douglas MacArthur's March 1948 endorsement. It continues with diplomatic and inter-departmental correspondence from July to September 1948 among the Far Eastern Commission, State Department, SANACC, and SCAP establishing Allied policy on access to Japanese scientific and technical information developed before 1946. The section concludes with SCAPIN 1925 and related GHQ administrative directives issued in August 1948 detailing pass procedures, technical investigation limits, and mission logistics for accredited Allied experts visiting Japanese industrial and research facilities.

subfiles.about: Presents recommendations for the comprehensive reorganization and democratization of scientific administration, higher education, professional societies, and industrial research in postwar Japan.
subfiles.from: Scientific Advisory Group (Roger Adams, W. D. Coolidge, Royal W. Sorensen, W. V. Houston, Merrill K. Bennett, William J. Robbins)
keywords: Commission on Higher Education and Research
Advisory Council on Higher Education and Research
subfiles.summary: This concluding portion of the Scientific Advisory Group report examines Japanese foreign trade and the importance of science in economic reconstruction. It reviews the Renewal Committee and recommends establishing an elected Advisory Council on Higher Education and Research and a governmental Commission on Higher Education and Research to coordinate policy and allocate research funds. The report also recommends strengthening nationwide professional societies, reforming university governance and the chair system, and preserving Zaibatsu industrial laboratories for peaceful development.
